_meta.indication: Treatment of adult patients with moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis whose disease is not adequately controlled with topical prescription therapies or when those therapies are not advisable; can be used with or without topical corticosteroids

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group monotherapy study; subjects randomized 1:1:1 to dupilumab 300 mg QW, 300 mg Q2W, or placebo
pivotal_trials.population: Adults 18 years of age or older with moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis not adequately controlled with or intolerant to topical prescription therapy
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of subjects achieving IGA 0 or 1 with a reduction of ≥2 points from baseline at Week 16
pivotal_trials.n: FAS 671 (300 mg QW 223, 300 mg Q2W 224, placebo 224)
pivotal_trials.result: IGA 0 or 1 at Week 16: 300 mg QW 37% (83/223), 300 mg Q2W 38% (84/224) vs placebo 10% (23/224); EASI 75: QW 53%, Q2W 51% vs placebo 15%; both dupilumab regimens superior to placebo (p<0.0001)

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group monotherapy study identical to Trial 1334; randomized 1:1:1 to dupilumab 300 mg QW, 300 mg Q2W, or placebo
pivotal_trials.population: Adults 18 years of age or older with moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis not adequately controlled with or intolerant to topical prescription therapy
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of subjects achieving IGA 0 or 1 with a reduction of ≥2 points from baseline at Week 16
pivotal_trials.n: FAS 708 (300 mg QW 239, 300 mg Q2W 233, placebo 236)
pivotal_trials.result: IGA 0 or 1 at Week 16: 300 mg QW 36% (86/239), 300 mg Q2W 36% (83/233) vs placebo 9% (20/236); EASI 75: QW 47%, Q2W 44% vs placebo 12%; both dupilumab regimens superior to placebo (p<0.0001)

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled adjunctive-therapy trial allowing concomitant topical corticosteroids; 740 subjects randomized 3:1:3 to dupilumab 300 mg QW+TCS, 300 mg Q2W+TCS, or placebo+TCS; 52 weeks of treatment
pivotal_trials.population: Adults 18 years of age or older with moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis, receiving dupilumab or placebo with concomitant topical corticosteroids for 52 weeks
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of subjects achieving IGA 0 or 1 at Week 16
pivotal_trials.n: FAS 740 (300 mg QW+TCS 319, 300 mg Q2W+TCS 106, placebo+TCS 315)
pivotal_trials.result: IGA 0 or 1 at Week 16: 300 mg QW+TCS 39% (125/319), 300 mg Q2W+TCS 39% (41/106) vs placebo+TCS 12% (39/315); EASI 75: QW+TCS 64%, Q2W+TCS 69% vs placebo+TCS 23% (p<0.0001)

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥1%): injection site reactions, conjunctivitis, blepharitis, oral herpes, keratitis, eye pruritus, other herpes simplex, dry eye. In the monotherapy trials: injection site reactions 10% vs 5% placebo; conjunctivitis 10% vs 2% placebo. In the DUPIXENT + TCS group: injection site reactions 10% vs 6% placebo+TCS; conjunctivitis 9% vs 5% placebo+TCS. Serious risks include hypersensitivity and conjunctivitis/keratitis.
target_moa: Human IgG4 kappa monoclonal antibody that binds the interleukin-4 receptor alpha chain (IL-4Rα), inhibiting both IL-4 and IL-13 signaling

rems.type: A REMS was not proposed and is not recommended; routine pharmacovigilance and labeling are sufficient

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee meeting was held for this application
